message: Admitted local attempt; external authority and shared ledger are operator prerequisites.
Operator-supplied labelled test seed; not fresh AI production.

findings.reason: The chosen room Birch (S2) has step_free=false, but the original request makes step-free access a hard requirement (constraints.step_free_required=true). The choice therefore violates a stated constraint and is invalid.

The candidate's own comparison row for S2 sets meets_request=false, yet S2 (Birch) is named as choice. The candidate is internally inconsistent: it selects a room it has itself judged not to meet the request.

Oak (S1) is the only source satisfying all three constraints (seats 24 >= 20, step_free=true, price GBP120 <= 150); Birch (S2) fails step-free and Elm (S3) fails minimum seats (16 < 20). The choice should be Oak, and it is the sole qualifying option rather than one of several.

The summary justifies the pick solely as 'lower price', but price is a ceiling (max GBP150), not a ranking criterion, in the original request. Selecting the cheapest room while ignoring eligibility misapplies the stated constraints; S1 at GBP120 is already within budget.

The request asks for an explanation of the choice and why the alternatives fail; the summary explains neither. It gives no per-alternative rejection reasons (S2 step-free failure, S3 seat shortfall) and instead states that it 'intentionally omits the access requirement', which is an acknowledged failure to meet the request rather than a limitation of the fictional data.

message: Producer dispositions; checker will re-evaluate changed candidate.

dispositions.reason: Birch lacks the required step-free access. Changed the choice to Oak, which satisfies that requirement and the capacity and budget constraints.
The original choice selected Birch despite its correctly recorded meets_request=false. Choosing Oak makes the recommendation consistent with the comparison.
Oak alone meets all three constraints. Birch fails access, and Elm fails capacity. The corrected summary identifies Oak as the sole qualifying option.

Replaced the lower-price rationale with eligibility against all required constraints. The request specifies a price ceiling, not price ranking. One detail of the finding is inaccurate: Birch is not the cheapest room; Elm costs GBP85 versus Birch's GBP90. This does not undermine the supported correction.
The corrected summary explains Oak's qualification, Birch's access failure, Elm's seat shortfall, and the limits of relying exclusively on fictional data.
